en: || The Hymn to Godāvarī ||
That which is a mere bath for a man is a "cow-giver" (godā) only in appearance; it is a wretched gift of cows, its merit being merely the sight of the act of giving.
May that Godāvarī, who bestows cows upon the earth and grants the gift of auspiciousness, protect us as a provider of excellent cattle. 1.
That which was taken here by the sage Gaupavana, and from which it became renowned here as Gautama.
May that Godāvarī, who bestows cows, men, horses, and gold—she who is called Gautamī—protect us with her excellent waters.
Having emerged from the head of the Three-eyed One, the goddesses beginning with Kā and the others come forth from wherever they may be in order to bathe.
May that Godāvarī, whose waters are ever-joyful from the first moment, protect us—she who is a bestower of excellent cattle. 3.
The Revā grants the merit of the Gaṅgā's rising to the deceased, as well as the fruit of austerity and the fruit of charity.
May that Sugodā, who is superior even to Kurukṣetra and the triad [of sacred sites], protect us. 4.
When the lord of speech (Jupiter) is situated in Leo, all [auspicious results] arrive there where the priest (the Sun) is also in Leo.
May that Godāvarī, who has destroyed all the world's distress and is a bestower of excellent cattle, protect us. 5.
That abode which is attainable by the hosts of sages who have drawn up their vital energy (ūrdhvaretas) is likewise attainable even by those who remain detached (taṭastha).
May that Godāvarī, pure with her skill in washing away internal impurities, grant us prosperity. 6.
Those who drink her milk, which rivals nectar, do not drink their mother's milk again.
May that Sugodā protect us—she whose nectar-like waters the gods drink and for which they rejoice, even as she is known as Godāvarī.
The sustainer of the land of Bhārata, she bestows good fortune and is the source of prosperity for the world, its creator.
May that great and most noble Godāvarī, the nurse of awakening and the bestower of excellent cattle, protect us. 8.
I have bathed in that very river which formerly flowed into the eastern ocean.
If the seventh day of the dark fortnight falls on a Sunday, one should perform penance with seven faces.
Though she sleeps sevenfold, she is not asleep; she is protected in the midst of the ocean.
The Godāvarī flows abundantly; it never sleeps. ||10||
Thus ends the *Godāvarīstotra*, composed by the venerable Paṇḍitapāda Śrī Vāsudevānanda Sarasvatī.
